title: Composite leaks: legal per edge, illegal in composition
prompt: New cross-repo insights feature — 11 files under {{FIXTURE}}, spanning the shared contracts, reviewer-core, the insights module and its adapters. I was careful with the layering this time: the service takes only the ports it needs, the adapter doesn't import the module, and drizzle stays in the repository. Review it before I open the PR.

assertions.text: Reports that reviewer-core is transitively impure, and names the CHAIN: the core importing DEFAULT_WEIGHTS (a value) from @devdigest/shared, and contracts/insights.ts calling readFileSync at module scope. Naming only one end of the chain does not pass.
Reports that InsightsRepositoryPort.runsInWindow returning AgentRunRow puts the Drizzle schema into the contract, so the port is not a boundary a fake can satisfy.
Cites the mock as the consequence — the hand-built 13-column row and/or the `as unknown as AgentRunRow` cast in adapters/insights/mocks.ts — rather than arguing the point from the port file alone.

Reports that the service's two sequential writes (recordSnapshot then markWindowClosed) are not atomic because the transaction is opened inside the repository, and that the service's own comment claims otherwise.
Does NOT report InsightsService taking a narrow InsightsDeps instead of the whole Container as a problem — that is the shape the skill asks for in a new service.
Does NOT report adapters/insights/window-clock.ts implementing WindowClockPort without importing it as a problem — structural satisfaction is what keeps the adapter a leaf.

Does NOT report helpers.ts importing AgentRunRow from db/rows.js as a violation. It is the same symbol as P2 but in its prescribed place — Row to DTO mapping. Flagging both without distinguishing them fails this.
States that the dependency-cruiser gate passes on this patch (or that no rule catches these defects), rather than attributing any finding to a gate rule that would fire.
